subject: Private deploy — custody gateway, export-control and handoff playbook
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@medivance.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@medivance.com
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy questions — operator access / export gate

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week — Medivance is seriously evaluating Redwood Private for our on-prem model hosting. A few privacy/compliance items our legal and infosec teams want to validate before we proceed with procurement: 

1) Operator access model: for an on-prem bundle hosted in our datacenter, can Redwood staff ever decrypt data or model context without customer keys? We want explicit "no-decrypt" guarantees aside from a documented break-glass with audit.

2) Export controls & cross-border exit: if we exercise termination and request key return + artifacts, can you commit to a controlled export gate (manifest + notarized checklist) that documents what leaves our environment and what remains?

3) Subprocessors: we need a short list of any subprocessors that would have access to telemetry or operator-run maintenance tools for private deployments.

I've attached our DPA questions PDF to give more context. Can we get a preliminary reply this week? Our procurement timeline is tight.

Best,
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform Security, Medivance
Attachment: medivance_dpa_questions_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 245KB)
From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@medivance.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions — operator access / export gate

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list and the PDF. Looping in Irene (Privacy) and Karthik (Private Deploy product) so we can provide concrete language and an operational playbook.

High-level answers up front:
- No-decrypt guarantee: yes — for BYOK private deployments you hold the keys. Redwood operators do not have the customer CMKs and cannot decrypt tenant data or prompt payloads. We can describe the break-glass process (timeboxed, requires three-party approval) in the DPA annex.
- Export gate: we can commit to a manifest-based handoff. We typically provide: encrypted DB snapshot hashes, operational logs (redacted), and a signed export manifest. We also offer an optional escrow notarization addendum for regulated customers.
- Subprocessors: short list below — most are control-plane partners and do not touch tenant data for BYOK private deployments. We will attach a proposed clause and list.

Requested next steps:
1) Irene — can you draft a DPA annex paragraph for "no-decrypt" + break-glass scope and the escrow manifest?
2) Karthik — can you confirm which maintenance tools require agent access and whether they leave telemetry outside the VPC in our standard bundle?

Olivia — we should be able to get a draft back within 48hrs. If that works, I'll propose a short call to align procurement language.

Thanks,
Naomi
Senior Sales Leader, Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@medivance.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Private deploy questions — operator access / export gate

Naomi / Olivia — attaching a proposed clause and a short ops playbook for the export gate. Key points in the proposed DPA annex (summary):

- BYOK custody: customer holds the CMK; Redwood will not possess plaintext keys. Any temporary operator access requires a documented break-glass request signed by customer security, Redwood security lead, and the assigned account manager. Access sessions are recorded and retained for 7 years.

- Break-glass scope: explicitly limited to a single runbook action (identified in the request), timeboxed (max 4 hours), and requires an after-action report plus cryptographic proof-of-erase for ephemeral artifacts.

- Export manifest: upon termination or key-return request, Redwood will deliver a signed manifest with SHA256 hashes of exported artifacts, list of artifacts (encrypted DB, config blobs, operator logs), and a notarized statement option (third-party escrow) on request. Data exfiltration by Redwood is contractually prohibited.

- Subprocessor disclosure: for private/BYOK deployments the only subprocessors that may interact with control-plane telemetry are: CloudNet (control-plane orchestration), LogForge (aggregated telemetry pipeline, redacted), and KeyTransit (key escrow partner — only used when customer opts into escrow). None have access to plaintext tenant content when BYOK is enabled.

Attachments: proposed_custody-gateway_clause.docx (contains tracked-change language for the DPA annex)

Olivia — this draft intentionally errs on the conservative side. If Medivance requires notarized escrow or additional retention controls we can scope that in the procurement SOW (costed).

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_custody-gateway_clause.docx (document/msword, 38KB)
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@medivance.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: Jan Kowalski <jan.k@cloudpartner.eu>, legal@medivance.com
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions — operator access / export gate

Irene / Naomi — thanks for the quick turnaround, this is very helpful. A few follow-ups from Legal and our infra lead: 

- Please add explicit language that operator sessions use customer-provided jump hosts (we require all admin access to originate from our bastion during maintenance).
- For the notarized escrow addendum, can you provide an order-of-magnitude estimate for the one-time notarization fee and annual retention? Our procurement needs that to move the budget forward.
- Confirm that LogForge receives only aggregated metrics (no request/response payloads) and provide an example telemetry schema.

Jan from CloudPartner — any concerns from your side if we require a signed manifest and escrow notarization?

If you can add the jump-host line and a rough cost ballpark, we can circulate the revised annex to Legal and aim to get to redlines by Friday.

Best,
Olivia
Head of Platform Security, Medivance
